title: Two Sum
hints: A brute force approach checks every pair. Can you do better?
Use a hash map to store each value's index as you iterate.
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

title: Add Two Numbers
hints: Think about how you would add two numbers using paper and pencil.
Traverse both lists and add corresponding digits with carry.
description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each node contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
hints: Use a sliding window approach with a hash set.
Track the last occurrence of each character to optimize the left boundary.
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
hints: The overall run time complexity should be O(log (m+n)).
Think about binary search on the smaller array.
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
hints: There are two approaches: dynamic programming and expanding around center.
Expanding around each character and each pair of characters gives O(n^2) time.
description: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.

title: Reverse Integer
hints: Think about how to handle overflow.
Use 64-bit integer for intermediate results.
description: Given a signed 32-bit integer x, return x with its digits reversed. If reversing x causes the value to go outside the signed 32-bit integer range, return 0.

title: Palindrome Number
hints: Negative numbers are never palindromes.
You can reverse the entire number and compare.
description: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome integer. An integer is a palindrome when it reads the same backward as forward.

title: Container With Most Water
hints: Try the two-pointer approach starting from the widest container.
Move the pointer pointing to the shorter line inward.
description: You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that holds the most water.

title: Roman to Integer
hints: Map each Roman numeral to its integer value.
Process from right to left, subtracting if the current value is less than the next.
description: Given a roman numeral, convert it to an integer.

title: Longest Common Prefix
hints: Use the first string as a reference and check each character against all others.
Vertical scanning is one approach.
description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.

title: 3Sum
hints: Sort the array first, then use a fixed pointer and two moving pointers.
Skip duplicates to avoid duplicate triplets.
description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
hints: Use backtracking to generate all combinations.
Map each digit to its corresponding letters.
description: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent.

title: Valid Parentheses
hints: Use a stack to track opening brackets.
When you see a closing bracket, check if the top of the stack is the matching opener.
description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
hints: Use a dummy head to simplify edge cases.
Compare nodes from both lists and attach the smaller one.
description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted list by splicing together the nodes.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
hints: Use a two-pointer approach: one for reading, one for writing.
Since the array is sorted, duplicates are always adjacent.
description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once.

title: Remove Element
hints: Use a two-pointer approach.
One pointer tracks where to place the next non-val element.
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer val, remove all occurrences of val in nums in-place.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
hints: Modify binary search to handle the rotation.
Determine which half of the array is sorted and search accordingly.
description: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values). The array is possibly rotated. Given a target, return its index or -1.

title: Search Insert Position
hints: Use binary search.
The answer is the position where the target would be inserted.
description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index if the target is found. If not, return the index where it would be inserted.

title: Trapping Rain Water
hints: For each bar, the water above it is min(left_max, right_max) - height.
Use two pointers to avoid precomputing left and right max arrays.
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

title: Permutations
hints: Use backtracking with a visited array or swap elements.
At each step, fix one element and recurse on the rest.
description: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all the possible permutations. You can return the answer in any order.

title: Rotate Image
hints: Transpose the matrix first, then reverse each row.
Think about the relationship between original and rotated positions.
description: You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise) in-place.

title: Group Anagrams
hints: Sort each string and use the sorted version as a key.
Use a hash map to group strings with the same sorted key.
description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.

title: Maximum Subarray
hints: This is Kadane's algorithm.
If the running sum drops below 0, reset it to the current element.
description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum and return its sum.

title: Merge Intervals
hints: Sort intervals by start time.
Iterate and merge overlapping intervals.
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals.

title: Climbing Stairs
hints: This is essentially a Fibonacci sequence.
dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2].
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
hints: Use the first row and first column as markers.
Use a separate flag for the first row and first column.
description: Given an m x n matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0.

title: Minimum Window Substring
hints: Use two pointers to create a sliding window.
Track the count of characters needed from t.
description: Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n respectively, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t is included in the window.

title: Subsets
hints: Use backtracking to include or exclude each element.
There are 2^n subsets for an array of n elements.
description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
hints: Use min and max bounds as you traverse.
Inorder traversal of a BST produces a sorted sequence.
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).

title: Same Tree
hints: Recursively compare the roots of both trees.
Both nodes must be null, or both must have the same value and matching children.
description: Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, write a function to check if they are the same or not.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
hints: Use recursion: max depth = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).
A null node has depth 0.
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
hints: Track the minimum price seen so far.
For each day, calculate the profit if you sell on that day.
description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy and a single day to sell.

title: Valid Palindrome
hints: Use two pointers from both ends.
Skip non-alphanumeric characters and compare case-insensitively.
description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
hints: Use a HashSet for O(1) lookups.
Only start counting from the beginning of a sequence (i.e., num-1 not in set).
description: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time.

title: Single Number
hints: XOR of a number with itself is 0.
XOR all numbers together; duplicates cancel out.
description: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one. You must implement a solution with linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.

title: Linked List Cycle
hints: Use Floyd's cycle detection algorithm (tortoise and hare).
Two pointers move at different speeds; if they meet, there's a cycle.
description: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it.

title: LRU Cache
hints: Combine a HashMap with a doubly linked list for O(1) operations.
The linked list maintains the access order.
description: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
hints: Track both the maximum and minimum product at each position.
A negative number can flip min to max.
description: Given an integer array nums, find a subarray that has the largest product and return the product.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
hints: Use binary search.
The minimum is at the pivot point where the rotation occurs.
description: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Given the rotated array nums, return the minimum element.

title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
hints: Use two pointers starting from the heads of both lists.
When a pointer reaches the end, redirect it to the other list's head.
description: Given the heads of two singly linked-lists headA and headB, return the node at which the two lists intersect.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
hints: Use two pointers from both ends of the sorted array.
Move the left pointer right to increase the sum, right pointer left to decrease.
description: Given a 1-indexed array of integers numbers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number.

title: Number of Islands
hints: Use DFS or BFS to explore each island.
Mark visited cells to avoid counting the same island twice.
description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.

title: Reverse Linked List
hints: Use three pointers: prev, current, next.
Iteratively redirect each node's next pointer to the previous node.
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
hints: Each node stores a map of children and a boolean for end-of-word.
For insert, create nodes as needed. For search/prefix, traverse character by character.
description: Implement a trie with insert, search, and startsWith methods.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
hints: Use a min-heap of size k.
Quickselect algorithm can solve this in average O(n) time.
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.

title: Invert Binary Tree
hints: Swap the left and right children of every node.
Use recursion or BFS.
description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
hints: Inorder traversal of a BST visits nodes in sorted order.
Count nodes as you traverse and stop at the kth.
description: Given the root of a binary search tree, and an integer k, return the kth smallest value (1-indexed) in the tree.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
hints: Use recursion to search both subtrees.
If both p and q are found in different subtrees, the current node is the LCA.
description: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes p and q.

title: Product of Array Except Self
hints: Build a prefix product array and a suffix product array.
The answer for each index is prefix_product * suffix_product.
description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

title: Sliding Window Maximum
hints: Use a deque to maintain indices of useful elements.
Remove indices outside the window and indices with smaller values.
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left to the very right. Return the max sliding window.

title: Valid Anagram
hints: Count character frequencies and compare.
If the strings have different lengths, they can't be anagrams.
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.

title: Move Zeroes
hints: Use a two-pointer approach.
One pointer tracks where to place the next non-zero element.
description: Given an integer array nums, move all 0's to the end while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
hints: Use DP: dp[i] = length of LIS ending at index i.
Binary search approach gives O(n log n) time.
description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Coin Change
hints: Use bottom-up DP: dp[i] = min coins to make amount i.
For each amount, try each coin and take the minimum.
description: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
hints: Count frequencies with a HashMap.
Use a bucket sort or a min-heap of size k.
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
hints: Use a HashSet for one array and check membership from the other.
Remember to return unique elements only.
description: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return an array of their intersection. Each element in the result must be unique.

title: Ransom Note
hints: Count character frequencies in both strings.
Check if magazine has enough of each character.
description: Given two strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed by using the letters from magazine.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
hints: This is a variant of the subset sum problem.
The target sum for each subset is total/2.
description: Given an integer array nums, return true if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of elements in both subsets is equal.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
hints: Use a sliding window and track the most frequent character.
window_length - max_frequency <= k means the window is valid.
description: You are given a string s and an integer k. You can replace at most k characters to make all characters the same. Return the length of the longest substring with all the same characters.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
hints: The diameter at each node is left_depth + right_depth.
Track the maximum diameter during DFS.
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter of the tree. The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
hints: Use prefix sums with a hash map.
For each prefix sum, check if (current_sum - k) has been seen before.
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to k.

title: Palindromic Substrings
hints: Expand around each center (character or pair of characters).
Count palindromes found during expansion.
description: Given a string s, return the number of palindromic substrings in it.

title: Binary Search
hints: Standard binary search: compare target with mid element.
Maintain left and right boundaries.
description: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, return its index, otherwise return -1.

title: Daily Temperatures
hints: Use a monotonic decreasing stack of indices.
When a warmer temperature is found, pop and calculate the difference.
description: Given an array of integers temperatures represents the daily temperatures, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after the ith day to get a warmer temperature.

title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
hints: dp[i] = min cost to reach step i.
At each step, you can come from 1 or 2 steps back.
description: You are given an integer array cost where cost[i] is the cost of ith step. Once you pay the cost, you can either climb one or two steps. Find the minimum cost to reach the top.

title: Partition Labels
hints: First, find the last occurrence of each character.
Use a greedy approach to expand each partition to include all characters within it.
description: You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part.

title: Middle of the Linked List
hints: Use the slow and fast pointer technique.
Slow moves one step, fast moves two steps. When fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle.
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node of the linked list. If there are two middle nodes, return the second middle node.

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
hints: The largest squares come from either end of the array.
Use two pointers from both ends and merge into a result array.
description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.
